detail: books/owner-config.lisp fn-ocfg-close decides whether the closing connection held the pending transaction by (equal (fn-own-pending (fn-ocfg-owner oc)) id). When nothing is pending, fn-own-pending is NIL, so a :close whose id is NIL matches it, and the staged configuration record (the configuration transaction lock) is cleared. Ground counterexample, evaluated on persvati by Codex lane p-reconfig-lock round 1 (/tmp/p-reconfig-lock-counterexamples.lisp on the laptop): (fn-ocfg-step (fn-ocfg-make (fn-own-start (fn-sn-initial nil 0) 2) (fn-cfg-initial) nil *fn-cfg-default-record*) '(:close nil) fn-arena) has fn-ocfg-staged NIL. This false statement is how it was found: the first form of fn-orl-staged-record-holds-the-configuration (books/owner-reconfig-lock.lisp, lane p-reconfig-phased) had no hypothesis on the :close id.
fix: Compare only a pending id that exists: (and (fn-own-pending (fn-ocfg-owner oc)) (equal (fn-own-pending (fn-ocfg-owner oc)) id)), or require (natp id) in fn-ocfg-close. Then drop the (implies (equal (car event) :close) (natp (cadr event))) hypothesis from fn-orl-staged-record-holds-the-configuration and fn-orl-reader-events-keep-the-authorization. The (:close nil) teeth in tests/acl2/owner-reconfig-lock-tests.lisp turn into positive witnesses, and the change recertifies owner-config's closure.
